title: EviCast: Forecasting Retrieval Gains Through Shared Response Calibration
abstract: arXiv:2611.02387v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) extends large language models with external evidence, yet relevant evidence does not ensure that a generator can use it. Indiscriminate retrieval can degrade task performance while adding retrieval and long-context inference costs. Existing methods neither determine before large-scale execution whether a generator, task distribution, and retriever configuration is worth deploying nor diagnose multiple candidate retrievers under a shared budget. We introduce EviCast, a framework that forecasts retrieval value through interventional evidence-state decomposition. EviCast measures a generator's response to controlled evidence states once and combines this shared profile with the offline evidence-state distribution of each candidate retriever, yielding the end-to-end net utility and its 95% lower confidence bound without executing every RAG configuration. translated_abstract: 检索增强生成（RAG）通过外部证据扩展了大语言模型的能力，然而相关证据并不能保证生成器能够有效利用它。不加区分的检索可能降低任务性能，同时增加检索和长上下文推理的成本。现有方法既无法在大规模执行之前判断某个生成器、任务分布和检索器配置是否值得部署，也无法在共享预算下诊断多个候选检索器。我们提出了EviCast，这是一个通过干预性证据状态分解来预测检索价值的框架。EviCast只需测量一次生成器对受控证据状态的响应，并将这一共享的响应特征与每个候选检索器的离线证据状态分布相结合，从而无需实际执行每个RAG配置即可得出端到端的净效用及其95%置信下界。状态细化分析刻画了其……（原文在此处被截断）
tldr: EviCast通过一次性测量生成器对受控证据状态的响应，并将其与各候选检索器的离线证据状态分布相结合，无需实际执行每个RAG配置即可预测检索的端到端净效用及置信下界。
en_tdlr: EviCast forecasts retrieval value by measuring a generator's response to controlled evidence states just once and combining this shared profile with each candidate retriever's offline evidence-state distribution, yielding end-to-end net utility and confidence bounds without executing every RAG configuration.
